description:
pkix-path/src/lib.rs:1157-1168 — find_cert_ext uses .ok() to discard parse errors:
  `.and_then(|e| T::from_der(e.extn_value.as_bytes()).ok())`

This function is correctly marked 'fail-open' and the comment says: 'Use this for extensions where a parse failure is tolerable. For security-critical extensions, use try_find_cert_ext instead.'

However, find_cert_ext is used for:
1. cert_subject_alt_names (line 1201) — used in NC checking and leaf SAN checks
2. TrustAnchor::from_cert (line 435) — for NameConstraints

If a CA cert has a critical NameConstraints extension that is malformed:
- TrustAnchor::from_cert (line 434-441) uses find_cert_ext, so the NC is silently dropped
- The doc says 'for strict RFC 5280 §4.2.1.6 compliance, use TrustAnchor::try_from'

For SubjectAltName in NC enforcement (cert_subject_alt_names), a malformed SAN is silently treated as absent. If the NC state requires an rfc822Name entry in SAN, a malformed SAN would pass the NC check (no names to check against). This is a security bypass:
- Set up: trust anchor with rfc822Name permitttedSubtree
- Attack cert: a cert with a malformed (not-parse-able) SAN extension — the malformed SAN is treated as absent, and the NC check passes

cert_name_constraints() at line 1212 correctly uses try_find_cert_ext for NC on certs. But cert_subject_alt_names at line 1200-1202 uses find_cert_ext (fail-open) for the SAN that is CHECKED against NC constraints.

A malformed SAN → None from find_cert_ext → no SAN names to check against NC → NC check passes even though the cert may have been trying to assert names.

P1 — security bypass via malformed SAN in NC enforcement.
title: find_cert_ext is fail-open: silently swallows decode errors on security-critical extensions
